clue.text: One's often suspended from tree for sin

definitions.meaning: the slow-moving tree mammal spends most of its life hanging upside down from branches
one of the seven deadly sins, idleness or laziness

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a hanging rainforest mammal and the deadly sin of idleness.

clue.text: Standard indicators of military rank

definitions.meaning: a standard is a flag, here the US national flag

explanation.definitionFit: The US flag is called this, and badges and chevrons on a uniform show rank.

clue.text: Old newspaper's taken on printing unit many times

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times newspaper
an en is a printers' measure of width

explanation.surface: An old newspaper takes on a printing machine.
explanation.walkthrough: An en is a unit of width in typesetting.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done frequently happens again and again.

clue.text: Collection of targets to be shot at?

definitions.text: Collection of targets to be shot at?

parts.words: Collection of targets to be shot at?
parts.note: reads like a set of range targets, but means a roster of people marked for killing or attack

explanation.definitionFit: A roll of people marked for elimination is the targets someone intends to strike.

clue.text: Philosophy of life enjoyed by astronauts

definitions.meaning: an overall outlook or personal philosophy
literally a view of the whole globe, as seen from orbit

explanation.definitionFit: An outlook on existence is a person's whole outlook, and from space a crew literally sees the entire planet.

clue.text: Cross, in a fashion

indicators.note: in means the letter is placed inside the word for fashion

parts.note: a fashion means a way, as in a manner of doing
a cross is the letter X

explanation.surface: Someone is angry, after a fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: being cross in a way is old British slang 'waxy', meaning angry.
explanation.definitionFit: Waxy is dated British slang for angry or in a temper.

clue.text: Fugitive given loaf and vegetable

parts.note: a fugitive is a runner
loaf and bean are both slang for the head

explanation.surface: An escaped prisoner is handed bread and greens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loaf' is not bread: 'use your loaf' is British slang for head, as is 'bean'.
explanation.definitionFit: A climbing plant with long green pods is grown as a garden vegetable.

clue.text: To deny responsibility for daughter is a serious undertaking

parts.note: a vow is a solemn promise

explanation.surface: Disowning a daughter is a weighty matter.
explanation.definitionFit: To repudiate something is to refuse to own or answer for it.

clue.text: Home oddly not included in extremely detailed list

parts.note: at home means in

indicators.note: included in means the scrambled letters go inside the word for extremely

parts.note: extremely means very

indicators.note: oddly suggests the word not is arranged in an odd order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A home was strangely left out of a very thorough catalogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Home' is IN (as in 'at home'); 'oddly' and 'included in' together hide the word not, jumbled, inside the word for extremely.
explanation.definitionFit: A full itemised record of goods or stock.

clue.text: Aid to steering in rain inspired new crew at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are muddled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fresh crew is inspired to steer through the rain at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' signals the anagram of INSPIRED NEW CREW, not a nautical setting.
explanation.definitionFit: A wiper clears the glass so a driver can see to steer in wet weather.

clue.text: Treatment for poison given soldier, one sounding alarm

parts.note: a soldier is a caste of ant, so soldier gives ANT
the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: sounding tells us the following word is to be heard, not spelt, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: a tocsin is an alarm bell

explanation.surface: Someone poisoned receives an antidote from a soldier who raises the alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounding' turns TOCSIN, an old word for an alarm bell, into its sound-alike TOXIN.
explanation.definitionFit: An antidote is a substance that counteracts a poison in the body.

clue.text: Number observed to be over five

indicators.note: to be over five is read as wrapping round the five, so one word goes over and around the other

parts.note: observed means seen
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Someone's age is noticed to be more than five.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be over' here means covering: SEEN goes over and round V to give SE-V-EN.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a whole number, one more than six.

clue.text: Provided with illumination, naturally, from paper set on fire

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
set on fire means lit

explanation.surface: A newspaper is used to light a fire, providing light.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper; 'naturally' points to light from the sky rather than lamps.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bathed in daylight is lit by the natural source in the sky.

clue.text: Refuse to provide exits

definitions.meaning: refuse, the noun, means rubbish or scraps left over
exits as departures, acts of going away

explanation.definitionFit: Leftover scraps are rubbish, and departures are acts of going away.

clue.text: Escape without beating, but get a shiner

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the escape word goes round the other

parts.note: flight is escape
a lashing is a beating, LASH

explanation.surface: Someone flees unharmed but ends up with a black eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is the old sense of outside. 'shiner' looks like a black eye but means something that shines: a torch.
explanation.definitionFit: A handheld electric torch shines a beam, so it is a thing that shines.

clue.text: Place of entertainment not far from West End hit

parts.note: not far means nigh

indicators.note: End here means the last letter of the word West, not the London district

parts.note: to hit is to club

explanation.surface: A venue near London's West End theatre district has a hit show.
explanation.walkthrough: The West End is London's theatre district, but 'End' picks the last letter of 'West', T.
explanation.definitionFit: A late-night venue offers dancing, drinks and shows as entertainment.

clue.text: Clobber learner, always getting stick

parts.note: clobber is British slang for clothes or kit, gear
L is for learner, as on L-plates
always means ever

explanation.surface: Hit the learner, always reaching for a stick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clobber' looks like a verb to hit but is British slang for kit or gear.
explanation.definitionFit: The gearstick in a car is the lever used to change gear.

clue.text: Romantic type in anguish without love? Right

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: anguish means woe
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: A lovesick person is in torment, lacking love, and asks if that is right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside: WOE goes round O to give WOOE, then R.
explanation.definitionFit: A suitor courting someone is a romantic sort.

clue.text: Succeeded with difficult piece of pottery

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, used in family trees
difficult means hard

explanation.surface: A potter succeeded with a tricky piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragment of broken earthenware is a shard.

clue.text: Device for catching fish, nothing less

indicators.note: less means the zero is taken away from the fish's name

parts.note: a dragonet is a small spiny fish
nothing is zero, O

explanation.surface: A gadget for catching fish is all that is needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fish' is not part of the definition: the dragonet, a small sea fish, loses O ('nothing less').
explanation.definitionFit: A dragnet is a trawling net, and figuratively a sweep for catching suspects.

clue.text: Corporation's provision for a blowout

definitions.meaning: corporation is an old humorous word for a paunch or pot belly
a reserve wheel carried in case of a burst on the road

explanation.definitionFit: A roll of fat round the waist and the reserve wheel in a car boot share the name.

clue.text: Going over information that's demanding immediate attention

indicators.note: over means covering, so the going word goes round the information

parts.note: going means exit
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Reviewing data that needs urgent attention.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: An exigent situation is pressing and urgent.

clue.text: Monarch turned to subject worthy of trust

indicators.note: turned means the two letters for the monarch are read backwards

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the monarch
subject to means liable to

explanation.surface: A king turns to one of his subjects he can rely on.
explanation.walkthrough: ER (Elizabeth Regina, the Queen) 'turned' gives RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dependable can be trusted to do what is expected.

clue.text: So-called champagne around noon — time still available

indicators.note: around means the champagne's nickname goes round the letter for noon

parts.note: Veuve Clicquot champagne is nicknamed the Widow, from the French veuve

explanation.surface: Champagne is served around midday while there is still time.
explanation.walkthrough: Veuve Clicquot is known as 'the Widow' (veuve is French for widow), hence 'so-called'.
explanation.definitionFit: An opening in a schedule is a free period still open for booking.

clue.text: Barrier restricts organised workers; in fact

indicators.note: restricts means the barrier confines the other word inside it

parts.note: a dam is a barrier
TU is a trade union, organised workers

explanation.surface: A barrier holds back the union, in fact.
explanation.definitionFit: A datum is a single piece of information or given fact.

clue.text: What comes before or after this boat

definitions.text: What comes before or after this boat

parts.words: What comes before or after this boat
parts.note: a racing shell rowed by a team of that size, the number preceding five and following three; its sound also suggests fore, meaning before

explanation.definitionFit: A rowing boat for a crew of this size takes its name from the number of oarsmen.

clue.text: Piano joined by a leading group for dance

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
the van, short for vanguard, is the leading group

explanation.surface: A pianist teams up with a front-rank band to play for dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a stately sixteenth-century court dance, also spelt pavane.

clue.text: Members weren't bent in this Fascist movement

definitions.text: Members weren't bent in this Fascist movement

parts.words: Members weren't bent in this Fascist movement
parts.note: members are legs, kept stiff and unbending in a marching style associated with fascist parades

explanation.surface: A political group's members refused to compromise.
explanation.definitionFit: This stiff-legged parade march was used by Nazi and Fascist troops.

clue.text: Person examining involvement of tsar with court

indicators.note: involvement suggests the letters are tangled together and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An investigator looks into a tsar's dealings with his court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involvement of' mixes TSAR and COURT together.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrutator is one who scrutinises, especially an official checking votes.

clue.text: Sailor holds on to old woman in river

indicators.note: holds on to means the sailor's word contains the other

parts.note: a tar is a sailor
old woman is slang for mother, MA

explanation.surface: A sailor keeps hold of his mother in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tamar is the river dividing Devon from Cornwall in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the river forming most of the Devon-Cornwall border.
